answer: An agent economy can price identity like a jetty prices docking space: every new agent must lock a stake that only decays back after a long history of useful work, so a sybil farm pays rent on each fake hull. Reputation should grow like yarrow in a field, slow to spread and quick to wither when abused, so one bad act burns the stake behind every linked identity. Proven work becomes a relic of trust: verifiable attestations build a non-transferable record, and cloning that record costs more than a thousand fresh puppets could ever harvest.
